request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient, a 46-year-old male, was admitted in 2006 with a 3.7 mm skin cancer on his left forearm. He had multiple recurrences which were treated with surgical resections, topical imiquimod, and intra-tumour IL-2 as per protocol. The patient was enrolled in IMM-101-001 study which resulted in a decreased rate of new disease however his condition worsened with lung metastases developed. Subsequently, he received ipilimumab on a clinical trial which showed a remarkable response, with most of the lesions resolving and a couple of visceral lesions remaining stable over 5 years.  
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
CONDITION AT DISCHARGE:
Stable with no acute problems.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
The patient is advised to follow up for further evaluation to monitor his health status. 

FOLLOW-UP RECOMMENDATIONS:
A follow-up with a specialist is recommended for ongoing care. 

MEDICATIONS:
None.

FUTURE TREATMENT PLAN:
To be decided upon specialist consultation. 

SUMMARY:
The patient, a 46-year-old male, was admitted with a 3.7 mm skin cancer on his left forearm that had recurred several times. He was treated with surgical resections, topical imiquimod and intra-tumour IL-2, however, his condition worsened and he was enrolled in a clinical trial. The patient received ipilimumab and had a remarkable response, with most of the lesions resolving and a couple of visceral lesions stable over 5 years. The patient will follow up with a specialist for ongoing care and treatment planning.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: C43**

The principal diagnosis is malignant melanoma of the skin of the left forearm, which falls under C43 (malignant melanoma of skin). The record calls it a "skin cancer," but the treatments (IMM-101 vaccine trial, ipilimumab) and the recurrence and metastatic pattern point to melanoma. The lung metastases are secondary sites and do not change the principal diagnosis.
